question: does the FD/adjoint ratio move toward 1 when one grid is refined at a time at the same physical state?

factors.one_factor: refine the adjoint source grid (blockMesh) while keeping the canonical state and the physical domain
factors.why: tests the solver discretization of the adjoint/source chain; the analytic comparison cancels the transfer, so any ratio movement is solver-side
factors.required_runs: one base run per level; FD rows reused when the injected physical state is identical
factors.note: a new blockMeshDict must keep the declared fixed domain and clearance profile

factors.one_factor: refine the canonical design grid (voxel 0.05 -> 0.025) with a regenerated fixture
factors.why: tests whether the design parametrization (support cells and direction shape) moves the ratio
factors.required_runs: full fixture regeneration (spec variant, canonical snapshot, injection) plus base runs; register only after the source-grid factor is judged

metric.secondary: epsilon plateau spread, sign, base gates
metric.decision: if a refined level moves every direction toward 1 without worsening the plateau, register that level as the qualified configuration; if ratios diverge or signs flip, PQ1 becomes No-Go and the adjoint formulation is revised

stop_conditions: one factor at a time; no simultaneous changes
a failed base gate is reported as failed, never dropped
no scalar correction is applied while the grid factor is unresolved

budget.note: primal+adjoint per level; FD rows reused only when the injected state is bit-identical
